In 1594 the unit only 'raided several Moldavian and Hungarian towns' (no land held); the Vinnytsia oblast is my reading of 'the vicinity of Bratslav'.

keyframe_review.note: 283.3 k km2 (bbox 25.0-34.5E, 47.3-54.3N): an envelope of Right-bank Ukraine and the Belarusian towns. Years: the infobox gives 1594-1596 and the page has the Cossack tabor surrounded at Lubny in May 1596 and Nalyvaiko handed over on 7 July 1596; Cliopatria's end in 1599 has no support (he died 21 April 1597, Severyn Nalyvaiko page). Extent: the page says the rebels 'took the cities of Bratslav, Husiatyn, Bar, Lutsk, Kaniv, Cherkasy and Slutsk, Babruisk, and Mahiliou' and that the rising 'engulfed most of Polish crown lands in Ukraine and Belarus'; it does not say Nalyvaiko held land as a state, and his one stated territorial demand was 'the lands between Southern Buh and Dniester rivers south of Bratslav'. The shape is therefore a soft raiding zone, to be drawn hatched and only for the two years. No infobox area on either page to compare. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1595..1596 from this entry's own 'valid for 1595-1596 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

ledger.note: 1594: Nalyvaiko leaves Polish service and raises the Cossacks. 'He left the service in 1594, and organized a paramilitary unit of unregistered cossacks in the vicinity of Bratslav' and raided Moldavian and Hungarian towns (Nalyvaiko Uprising page: 'Nalyvaiko left Polish service in 1594'); infobox 1594-1596.

region.text: Lutsk, where the Cossacks 'massacred Polish nobility'

ledger.note: 1595: the Cossacks capture Lutsk (the page's 'following year' after 1594; the Severyn Nalyvaiko page has the same sentence and names no year).

region.text: 'the cities of Bratslav, Husiatyn, Bar, Lutsk, Kaniv, Cherkasy'

ledger.note: 1595: the Right-bank towns taken (the page lists them without years: 'took the cities of Bratslav, Husiatyn, Bar, Lutsk, Kaniv, Cherkasy and Slutsk, Babruisk, and Mahiliou'). Year bridged from the 1594-1596 span; the page is silent on the order.

region.text: Mahiliou and Babruisk; Slutsk lies in the Minsk oblast

ledger.note: 1595-1596: the Cossacks move into Belarus. 'From Volhynia Nalivaiko's Cossacks moved into Belarus, where they pillaged Mogilev' (Severyn Nalyvaiko page: no date). A raid, not a held province; the year is bridged and the region is my reading of the town list.

1596: the Cossack tabor surrenders. 'In May 1596 the Cossack tabor was surrounded by Polish forces near the town of Lubny' (two weeks of fighting on the Severyn page) and 'on 7 July 1596 Nalyvaiko was handed over by the Cossacks to the Poles as a condition of surrender'. He died in Warsaw on 21 April 1597.

1596: the rising is crushed. The conflict 'was ultimately won by the Crown of Poland'; the infobox gives '1594-1596' and 'Polish-Lithuanian victory'; afterwards 'all Cossack lands were taken and given to the Polish magnates'.

wars.name: Nalyvaiko Uprising
wars.outcome: Polish-Lithuanian victory: the Cossack tabor was surrounded at Lubny in May 1596 and Nalyvaiko was handed over on 7 July 1596; the Zaporozhian hetman Loboda had joined him and was later murdered.
wars.note: The page says the royal army also campaigned in Moldavia in support of Ieremia Movila's claim; the Tsardom of Muscovy and the Habsburgs figure only as would-be patrons of the Cossacks against the Turks and neither fought.

wars.name: Nalyvaiko's raids on Moldavia
wars.outcome: The unit 'raided several Moldavian and Hungarian towns' in 1594; no land changed hands.

certainty.note: A raiding zone, not a frontier: the pages name towns, not boundaries, and the rebels held no territory as a state.

notes:
Written 2026-10-31 by the eu-16-h agent from 2 pages (the budget).

Cliopatria row: 'Nalyvaiko Uprising', 1595..1599, one shape of 283 k km2. Both pages date the rising to 1594-1596, so the dossier runs 1594..1596 (July) and the shape is marked valid for 1595-1596 only. The row is a rebel state in the sense of rule 5 only loosely: neither page says the rebels held land or an administration; they 'took the cities' and the rising 'engulfed most of Polish crown lands in Ukraine and Belarus'. The rendering should draw the shape hatched and soft, or not at all; the reviewer should decide whether the row deserves a rebel colour.

Dates the pages do not give: the year of the Right-bank and Belarusian captures (1595 and 1595-1596 here are bridging, confidence 1); the year of Lutsk (implied 1595); the execution day (the lead gives only 'died 21 April 1597'); the Battle of Bila Tserkva and Solonytsia (not mentioned). Kyiv and Kremenchuk, which other accounts give, are not on the pages opened and are not recorded.

Counterparts: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (the loser of the land and the winner), Zaporozhian Cossacks (Loboda; slug zaporozhian-cossacks is in the group's other part), Principality of Moldavia (the 1594 raids). The Tsardom neighbours the shape in the seed's list but is not involved on the pages. No capital: the host had none on the pages (identity.capitals is empty).
